picks.intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager, CROSSCHECK-001)
picks.rationale: This is the one on-axis lever that doesn't make an 85%-blast patient wait weeks for a cell product to be manufactured, and with peripheral blasts climbing 58 to 82% in a month, wait time is the whole game. The preclinical package is genuinely strong for a phase 1 asset: sub-nanomolar killing across a range of antigen density, survival benefit in a primary-AML PDX at doses as low as 0.005 mg/kg, and no activation against normal neutrophils, CD34+ cells, or PBMCs (doi:10.1182/blood-2024-201699). The upside I'm buying: a T-cell engager that debulks refractory marrow fast and bridges to the second transplant that actually cures. I'm not pretending this is proven; it is first-in-human with zero efficacy readout, it needs the same pending A*02:01 typing as the rest of the axis, and CRS is a real class risk.
primary_concerns: First-in-human phase 1 with no efficacy or safety readout yet; the strong signal is all preclinical, one of which is an ASH abstract not a full paper
Gated on the still-pending HLA-A*02:01 typing; if the patient is A*02:01-negative the whole pick collapses
Cytokine release syndrome is the expected class toxicity and organ/cardiac fitness is undocumented
CG1 antigen density on this patient's blasts is not established

picks.intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning) to second allo-HCT
picks.rationale: For a marrow this hot, the boldest move that still has randomized evidence behind it is targeted radioimmunotherapy that carries active disease straight into a transplant rather than waiting for a remission that FLAG-IDA/venetoclax already failed to produce. SIERRA hit a durable CR of 17.1% versus 0% for conventional care (pmid:39298738), and it did it in exactly the age-appropriate active-R/R-AML population, with grade 3+ toxicity essentially matched to control. The upside is the only thing on this list with a real shot at cure: get to HCT2, then layer HLA-restricted consolidation on top. The honest caveat is that SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a first transplant, so second-HCT eligibility has to be confirmed, and OS was flat because half the control arm crossed over.
primary_concerns: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients; prior allo-HCT eligibility for the go-forward conditioning study (NCT07157514) must be verified
OS was not improved (HR 0.99) in the trial, driven by heavy crossover
Second transplant on an 85%-blast marrow with adverse cytogenetics carries substantial non-relapse mortality; organ function undocumented
Extramedullary thigh sarcoma may need directed radiotherapy that CD45 RIT will not fully cover

picks.intervention_label: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform / TSC-100 class), post-HCT
picks.rationale: This is the closest published precedent for the primary reason the case was submitted, and it delivered 4 of 9 CRs with no dose-limiting toxicities in exactly the post-transplant relapse setting (pmid:38683966). The mechanism is the graft-versus-leukemia effect aimed at a recipient-restricted antigen, so it can reach leukemia while largely sparing the tissues that drive GVHD; one patient stayed in remission past two years. My upside case is durable, HCT2-consolidating cellular immunity that turns a second transplant into a cure rather than a bridge. It is gated on A*02:01 plus a recipient HA-1-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch that neither the patient nor the sibling has been genotyped for, and n=9 is a thin efficacy base.
primary_concerns: Eligibility gated on A*02:01 AND a recipient-positive/donor-negative HA-1 mismatch, none genotyped yet in either the patient or the sibling donor
n=9 feasibility cohort, not powered for efficacy
Requires a fresh allo-HCT platform and recipient-origin relapse confirmed by sorted-CD34 STR chimerism before it is even applicable
Manufacturing lead time is a liability given the pace of this relapse

picks.intervention_label: CD123-CD33 compound CAR-T (dual-antigen, iCell cCAR, NCT04156256)
picks.rationale: This patient carries both CD33 and CD123 and is visibly evolving clonally at relapse, so a dual-antigen construct is the antigen-escape hedge the single-target agents don't give you. Preclinically the compound CAR beat single-antigen targeting for survival across four AML xenograft models and killed each antigen-positive population (pmid:29515236). The upside is deep cytoreduction that covers two targets at once ahead of transplant. Weaknesses are real: xenograft-only data, no post-allo-HCT experience, CAR-T-grade CRS, and an unclear registry/eligibility status.
primary_concerns: Preclinical evidence only; no clinical efficacy or safety readout in humans
CAR-T after a prior transplant raises its own eligibility, CRS, and myelosuppression concerns
Recruitment/registry status listed as unknown; access may not be real
Manufacturing lead time competes with a fast-moving relapse

picks.intervention_label: Rezatapopt (PC14586, Y220C-selective p53 reactivator) + venetoclax, myeloid trial NCT06616636
picks.rationale: If the pending NGS lands on TP53 Y220C, this is a variant-matched targeted shot with a clean mechanistic story: rezatapopt refolds the Y220C mutant and, paired with venetoclax, restores real apoptotic killing in Y220C AML (pmid:40608889). The solid-tumor readout shows a 30% response in Y220C/KRAS-wild-type disease (pmid:41740031), which is a meaningful signal for a p53-reactivator. I'm ranking it low because the contingency is double: the TP53 aberration has to be confirmed, then confirmed as Y220C specifically, and neither is resolved. Single-agent activity in myeloid disease looks weak, so it would need the venetoclax partner.
primary_concerns: Double contingency: TP53 status unresolved (2019 mutant vs 2026 negative on a limited assay), and Y220C not established
All clinical response data are in solid tumors; the myeloid trial has no results
Needs a venetoclax partner for apoptosis, and the patient just progressed on a venetoclax-containing regimen
Not cytoreductive fast enough alone for an 85%-blast marrow

picks.intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123 ADC) monotherapy
picks.rationale: As a CD123-directed debulking option this has actual single-agent clinical activity in R/R AML (ORR 21%, CI 8-40; CR 17%, CI 6-36 at the RP2D; pmid:38423051) and picomolar preclinical potency with a wide window over normal progenitors (pmid:29661755). The upside is a lower-drama, off-the-shelf way to knock the marrow down toward a transplant if the cellular routes stall on typing. I keep it toward the bottom because the response depth is modest and the veno-occlusive-disease signal is exactly the wrong toxicity to carry into a planned second transplant.
primary_concerns: VOD signal is a serious liability peri-transplant given the HCT2 plan
Modest single-agent depth (ORR ~21%); unlikely to be curative on its own
Benefit-predictive quantitative CD123 antigen density still pending
One treatment-related death in the escalation cohort

notes: Persona prior applied: I weight upside and accept thin evidence for large potential effect. The primary HLA-A*02:01 axis is unresolved but the resolving test is a records pull plus 3-7 day typing, so I refuse to foreclose it. CBX-250 ranked 1 on the off-the-shelf speed advantage for a fast-moving 85%-blast marrow plus a strong preclinical package, with eyes open on its first-in-human status. No toxicity vetoes in preferences.json, so nothing is excluded on veto grounds; I flag CRS (CBX-250, cCAR) and VOD (pivekimab, and by class gemtuzumab) as the toxicities to fit against undocumented organ function rather than to reject outright. Eprenetapopt deliberately not picked: pan-reactivator, phase 3 MDS miss, flagged low-yield. Menin inhibitors out of scope (KMT2A amplification is not a rearrangement).

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) for relapse after first allo-HCT
picks.rationale: A second transplant is the one curative move on this slate with a real registry behind it rather than a first-in-human hope. The Christopeit/Schmid EBMT series (pmid:23918951) is 179 second transplants; the matched-sibling subgroup that fits this patient ran ~37% 2-year OS, and her ~6-year remission after HCT1 sits on the favorable side of that curve. The toxicity here is not a mystery. NRM, GVHD, and infection are the known hazards, and every transplant unit has a worked-out management algorithm for each. What I want settled before signing off is fitness: no cardiac or organ-function numbers are documented, and 85% marrow blasts with an extramedullary thigh lesion argue for cytoreduction first rather than transplanting into florid disease. Rank 1 because it carries the curative intent on the best-characterized safety footing in the dossier, not because it is gentle.
primary_concerns: Fitness and organ-function data are absent; NRM in a post-HCT1 patient turns on cardiac/hepatic/renal reserve that has not been measured
Transplanting into 85% blasts is a poor bet; this needs cytoreduction to a lower burden first
GVHD risk on a second graft, compounded if a donor change is pursued
Registry OS (~37% at 2 years, sibling subgroup) is honest but not high; roughly half who reach CR relapse again

picks.intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab, anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning)
picks.rationale: This is the highest-tier evidence in the whole dossier and it earns a safety-first ranking on that alone. SIERRA (pmid:39298738) is a randomized phase 3: durable CR 17.1% vs 0% (p<0.0001), EFS HR 0.23. The number that matters most to me is the toxicity comparison, and it is reassuring: grade >=3 treatment-related AEs were 59.7% on apamistamab versus 59.2% on conventional care, so the targeted conditioning did not add net high-grade toxicity for the cytoreduction it bought. It gives a defensible route to carry an 85%-blast marrow into HCT2 without simply repeating the FLAG-IDA chemistry that already failed. Two caveats keep this out of rank 1: SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a FIRST transplant, so prior-HCT eligibility is unverified, and marrow-directed radioimmunotherapy may not touch the extramedullary thigh sarcoma.
primary_concerns: Prior-allo-HCT eligibility unverified; SIERRA was a first-transplant population, so this is an extrapolation
OS was flat (HR 0.99), plausibly from ~52% control crossover; the durable-CR benefit did not read through to survival
Marrow-directed RIT likely does not address the extramedullary thigh disease
Adds a radiation-conditioning hit on top of HCT2 in a patient whose organ reserve is undocumented

picks.intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Mylotarg, CD33 ADC)
picks.rationale: When I weight toxicity this heavily, an FDA-approved agent with more than twenty years of post-marketing safety and a fully worked-out AE-management playbook beats a novel mechanism I cannot yet characterize. CD33 is confirmed on the blasts, and the Sievers pooled phase 2 (pmid:11432892) gives a clean per-grade toxicity picture: G>=3 hyperbilirubinemia 23%, transaminase elevation 17%, no cardiotoxicity, low mucositis (4%). The class risk is hepatic veno-occlusive disease, and that is exactly the risk that has an established mitigation pathway (fractionated dosing, VOD surveillance, defibrotide on hand) rather than an open question. I am honest that single-agent depth in first relapse was only ~30% and this patient is further along than that population, so I position it as a predictable, manageable cytoreduction lever ahead of HCT2, not as a curative move on its own. Quantitative CD33 density is still pending and should gate the commitment.
primary_concerns: Hepatic VOD is the black-box class risk and it lands squarely in the peri-transplant window; fractionated dosing and VOD surveillance are mandatory, not optional
Single-agent remission was ~30% in a LESS pretreated first-relapse cohort; expect lower after FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure
Benefit is CD33-density-dependent and quantitative flow has not been done
Does not address the extramedullary thigh sarcoma

picks.intervention_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) from the sibling donor
picks.rationale: DLI has decades of registry experience and a single, well-understood toxicity in GVHD, which every transplant program manages with an established steroid-and-escalation algorithm. That maturity is why it earns a slot on a safety-first slate. The Schmid EBMT registry (pmid:17909197) is clear-eyed about who benefits: relapse >5 months after HCT (this patient ~6 years) favors it, and DLI beat no-DLI (2-year OS 21% vs 9%, P=0.04). But the same data show the benefit concentrates in patients treated in remission or with favorable karyotype (~56% 2-year OS), while active high-burden disease like this drops to ~15%. That is the honest read: DLI alone into 85% blasts and adverse cytogenetics is low-yield. I rank it here as a well-characterized adjunct to be given AFTER cytoreduction, not as a standalone.
primary_concerns: GVHD is the defining toxicity; manageable but real, and additive to any HCT2 GVHD risk
Low yield as a standalone in active high-burden disease (~15% 2-year OS in the active-disease subgroup); needs cytoreduction first
Adverse cytogenetics (MECOM, KMT2A amplification) put this patient in the worse-prognosis DLI subgroup
Requires confirmed recipient-derived relapse on CD34-sorted STR chimerism before proceeding

picks.intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager, CROSSCHECK-001)
picks.rationale: I am ranking this last and flagging it, not endorsing it. The preclinical package (doi:10.1182/blood-2024-201699) is genuinely strong: sub-nanomolar killing across a range of antigen density, no activity against normal neutrophils, CD34+ cells, or PBMCs, and off-the-shelf delivery with no cell-manufacturing wait. What keeps it at the bottom of MY list is a specific missing safety datum, not novelty for its own sake: CROSSCHECK-001 (nct:NCT06994676) is first-in-human with no MTD established and no characterized adverse-event profile in a single treated patient. As a CD3 T-cell engager the anticipated class toxicity is cytokine release syndrome, and CRS severity scales with tumor burden, which in an 85%-blast marrow is the worst-case setting to meet an uncharacterized engager. There is no published human CRS-management experience for this specific agent to lean on. I would not advance it ahead of cytoreduction, and I would want it only after the burden is brought down and HLA-A*02:01 is confirmed. Pre-emptive statement for round 2: if this is nominated as a rank-1 or front-line pick over the transplant/cytoreduction backbone, I will dissent on evidence maturity, and I would move to a toxicity veto contingent on there being no CRS-mitigation plan (step-up dosing, tocilizumab availability, burden reduction first) documented for the high-blast setting.
primary_concerns: First-in-human with NO established MTD and NO characterized AE profile in any treated patient; the missing datum is a human safety readout, full stop
CD3-engager cytokine release syndrome scales with tumor burden, and 85% marrow blasts is the highest-risk CRS setting to debut an uncharacterized engager
No agent-specific CRS-management experience published to guide dosing, monitoring, or rescue
Gated on still-pending HLA-A*02:01 typing, so eligibility is not even established yet

notes: My prior weights toxicity heavily (efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.75 is documented as provisional pending an explicit fitness/goals-of-care assessment, and I read the missing cardiac/organ-function data as a reason to hold that weight loosely). So I built the slate around what carries curative intent on the best-characterized safety footing: HCT2 (registry-anchored, known NRM/GVHD algorithms), Iomab-B (phase 3, G>=3 TRAE non-inferior to conventional care), gemtuzumab (20+ years post-marketing, VOD with an established mitigation pathway), and DLI (decades of experience, GVHD as the single known toxicity). toxicity_vetoes is empty, so nothing here trips a HARD stop, and I have issued no formal veto in round 1. CBX-250 is ranked last deliberately: the preclinical data are strong but the specific missing datum is a human safety readout (no MTD, no AE profile), and a T-cell engager meeting an 85%-blast marrow is the exact CRS-scaling scenario I am most cautious about. I flagged, in the rank-5 rationale, a round-2 veto CONTINGENT on the absence of a documented CRS-mitigation plan for the high-burden setting; that conditional is load-bearing and I want it preserved. I did not rank rezatapopt (double biomarker contingency, zero myeloid clinical data, needs a venetoclax partner she has already failed) or eprenetapopt (flagged low-yield, phase 3 miss) or the dual cCAR (xenograft-only, CRS plus on-target myeloablation, unclear registry status); each is a real option but none clears my safety-evidence bar for a top-5 slot this round. HA-1 TCR-T is the stated priority handle and I respect that, but it is double-gated on ungenotyped HLA/HA status and n=9 feasibility data, so it does not earn a conservative top-5 on maturity grounds this round.

picks.intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab, anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning)
picks.rationale: SIERRA is the one randomized phase 3 in this whole set (PMID 39298738, tier 1b, RoB2 Some), and it hit its registered primary endpoint: durable CR 17.1% vs 0%, p<0.0001, which is exactly the problem this 85%-blast marrow poses, getting active disease into a transplant. What keeps it off a clean endorsement is that ITT OS was flat (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.7-1.41, p=0.96) once 52% of the control arm crossed over, so the durable-CR win is a surrogate, not a survival claim. SIERRA also enrolled patients heading to a FIRST transplant, and this patient needs an HCT2, so eligibility is an extrapolation the phase 3 does not cover.
primary_concerns: RoB2 deviations-from-intervention / measurement: open-label conditioning and a surrogate (durable CR at >=180 days) rather than OS
generalizability: enrolled first-transplant candidates, so the HCT2 setting is off-protocol and unverified
the OS null under 52% crossover means the effect on the endpoint patients care about is unproven

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT
picks.rationale: The evidence here is a retrospective EBMT registry (PMID 23918951, ROBINS-I Serious), not a trial, but it is large (n=179) and directly on-point: ~37% 2-year OS in the related-donor subgroup that matches this matched-sibling patient. The long first remission (~6 years) sits on the favorable side of the registry's own survival drivers. I rank it second rather than first only because a registry cohort cannot adjust away confounding-by-indication the way a randomized comparison would, and the 85%-blast active-disease burden at HCT2 pulls hard against that 37% figure.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I confounding: who gets an HCT2 is selected on fitness and disease control, which inflates the apparent survival
the 37% is a subgroup estimate, and this patient's active high-burden disease is the adverse tail of it, not the middle
no per-term NRM/toxicity breakdown in the source abstract

picks.intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Mylotarg, CD33 ADC)
picks.rationale: This is the only on-label, primary-indication option in the set for the patient's confirmed CD33 positivity, which is why it clears the others on regulatory footing. But the depth is honest and modest: pooled single-arm phase 2 (PMID 11432892, ROBINS-I Serious), ~30% CR+CRp, and the population was CD33+ first relapse with no antecedent hematologic disorder, meaning less pretreated than this FLAG-IDA/venetoclax-refractory patient with extramedullary disease. CR+CRp is a surrogate with no randomized comparator, and the calicheamicin VOD signal is not trivial with an HCT2 planned. I would want quantitative CD33 antigen density before leaning on it, since single-arm ADC response tracks density.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I: pooled single-arm, no comparator; CR+CRp is a surrogate
population mismatch: first-relapse, treatment-naive-marrow patients, not this refractory/post-transplant/extramedullary state, so the ~30% likely overstates the achievable rate here
hepatic/VOD class risk peri-HCT2; benefit-predictive CD33 density still only qualitative

picks.intervention_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) for AML relapse after allo-HCT
picks.rationale: The DLI registry does carry an adjusted signal (PMID 17909197, ROBINS-I Serious): 2-year OS 21% vs 9%, p=0.04 after multivariate adjustment, and this patient's very late relapse (~6 years) is on the favorable side of the timing driver. The catch is that the benefit concentrates in a subgroup he is not in: DLI given in remission or with favorable karyotype reached ~56% 2-year OS, while DLI in active/high-burden disease sat at ~15%, which is where an 85%-blast marrow with adverse cytogenetics lands him. This is a confounding-by-indication-prone comparison, so I read it as an argument for cytoreduction before any DLI, not for DLI alone.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I confounding-by-indication: DLI recipients were selected for lower burden and better performance
the favorable estimate is a subgroup this patient does not belong to; his active-disease subgroup is ~15% 2-year OS
unadjusted vs adjusted subgroup contrasts from a registry, not a randomized signal

picks.intervention_label: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform)
picks.rationale: I am ranking the marquee cellular option last on purpose, and the reason is evidence maturity, not biology. The closest published human data are n=9, single-arm phase 1 (PMID 38683966, ROBINS-I Serious), reported as 4/9 CR with 0 DLTs, which is a feasibility and safety readout, not an efficacy estimate you can size a decision on, and I could not retrieve the per-term AE table for it. Eligibility is doubly gated on pending HLA-A*02:01 typing plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative genotype in both patient and sibling, none of which is resolved. The related TCR-T trials (TSC-100/101 NCT05473910, BSB-1001 NCT06704152) are all phase 1 with no efficacy readouts, so the whole axis is early-phase behind a biomarker gate.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I Serious on an n=9 feasibility cohort: no efficacy powering, no comparator, per-term safety table unretrievable
double eligibility contingency (HLA-A*02:01 + HA-1 recipient-positive/donor-negative genotyping of both parties) all unresolved
CR proportion from 9 patients is not a stable effect estimate; wide uncertainty regardless of point value

notes: Re-run over the full current option set after cbx-250 was added. Ranked strictly on evidence quality, downstream of the confirmatory workup (HLA typing, TP53/Y220C resolution, quantitative CD33/CD123 density, sorted-CD34 STR chimerism). Iomab-B rank-1 as the only randomized phase-3 anchor (SIERRA, tier 1b) despite its surrogate endpoint and OS-null-under-crossover; transplant/DLI backbone next on large registries with the confounding named; gemtuzumab as the on-label single-arm floor; HA-1 TCR-T last on maturity/eligibility, not biology. NOT RANKED and why: cbx-250 (CBX-250, CROSSCHECK-001 NCT06994676) is the LEAST clinically-evidenced option in the whole set. Its human data are a phase-1 trial-in-progress with zero efficacy or safety readout (conference trial-in-progress abstract, no PMID, DOI unverifiable per the dossier's own fail-closed note), and everything supporting it is preclinical, an ASH 2024 abstract (DOI 10.1182/blood-2024-201699, PDX + cell lines, no PMID, conference-abstract level). Strong preclinical potency (sub-nM EC50, PDX survival benefit down to 0.005 mg/kg) does not move me without any clinical confirmation, and it is doubly contingent on the same pending HLA-A*02:01 typing. I decline to rank it above any option with a human readout; mechanism elegance is not evidence. rezatapopt deliberately unranked: cross-tumor-only (solid-tumor PYNNACLE, PMID 41740031, ORR 20%; all responders KRAS-wild-type), double biomarker contingency (confirm TP53 aberration, then confirm Y220C, both open on a 2%-LOD/no-CNV relapse panel), and the myeloid trial NCT06616636 has no results. eprenetapopt unranked: pan-reactivator, phase-3 in TP53-mutant MDS MISSED its primary endpoint and the program is on hold, plus a frontline line-mismatch. The CD123 agents (pivekimab PMID 38423051 ORR 21% 95% CI 8-40 at RP2D n=29; flotetuzumab and vibecotamab both program-discontinued) and dual CD33/CD123 CAR-T sit below the ranked five on either program status or single-arm depth; I did not force them into the five. Schema-validated. No git add/commit/push.

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT
picks.rationale: ELN 2022 (Dohner, Blood 2022;140:1345) puts a second allo-HCT at the center of curative-intent management for AML that relapses after transplant, conditioned on getting the marrow back into remission first. Her ~6-year first remission is the favorable variable: in the EBMT related-donor subgroup that maps to roughly 37% 2-year OS after HCT2 (Christopeit 2013), better than the cohort overall. NCCN AML v3.2026 keeps second transplant among the category 2A options for post-transplant relapse in fit patients, and ECOG 1 with no vetoed modality keeps her inside that population. It is the platform the rest of the plan, including any HLA-restricted consolidation, has to be built on.
primary_concerns: 85% marrow blasts plus a thigh myeloid sarcoma mean HCT2 cannot be delivered up front; the guideline recommendation is explicitly conditioned on cytoreduction first, which is the unsolved step here.
No cardiac or organ-function labs are on file, so the fitness assumptions ELN/NCCN attach to a second transplant are unverified.
TP53-aberrant complex-karyotype disease escaped graft-versus-leukemia once already; a durable HCT2 is far from assured even with a good first remission.

picks.intervention_label: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley/TSC-100 platform)
picks.rationale: Both NCCN AML v3.2026 and ELN 2022 name clinical-trial enrollment as the preferred route in relapsed/refractory AML, and this handle is the stated reason for the run: HA-1-directed donor TCR-T (TSC-100, NCT05473910; Fred Hutch platform, pmid 38683966). The phase 1 signal is early but real, with 4 of 9 recurrent post-HCT patients reaching or holding CR and no dose-limiting toxicity. It slots onto an HCT2 as consolidation, which is where the guideline-endorsed adoptive-cell approach for post-transplant relapse actually lives. I rank it second rather than first because eligibility is undetermined, not established.
primary_concerns: Eligibility is gated on HLA-A*02:01 plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch, and neither the patient nor the sibling donor has been genotyped; she sits in an undetermined enrolling population, not a confirmed-eligible one.
The guideline support is for 'enroll in a trial,' not for TCR-T as such; this is a phase-1 investigational product with no consensus category behind it.
It is post-transplant consolidation, so it does nothing for the 85%-blast marrow that has to be controlled first.

picks.intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Mylotarg, CD33 ADC)
picks.rationale: Gemtuzumab is the one on-label, guideline-listed drug in play: NCCN AML v3.2026 carries single-agent gemtuzumab (category 2A) for CD33-positive relapsed AML, and her blasts are CD33+ by flow. I read it as a cytoreductive bridge toward HCT2, not as definitive therapy. The honest ceiling is modest, about 30% overall remission in first relapse (Sievers 2001, pmid 11432892), and she is well past first relapse with extramedullary disease. Quantitative CD33 density is still pending, and that is the readout that tells us whether ADC-level expression is even there.
primary_concerns: The single-agent remission figure comes from a first-relapse population less pretreated than this patient; carrying it over to post-FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure with a myeloid sarcoma overstates likely benefit.
Calicheamicin hepatotoxicity and VOD are the class risk and matter directly with an HCT2 planned soon after (Sievers reported grade 3+ hyperbilirubinemia in 23%).
Qualitative CD33 positivity is not antigen density; committing before the quantitative flow is target selection done backwards.

picks.intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic bispecific T-cell engager targeting CG1/HLA-A*02:01)
picks.rationale: Trial enrollment is the preferred route in R/R AML under both NCCN AML v3.2026 and ELN 2022, and CBX-250 is a recruiting phase-1 on the patient's own A*02:01 axis (CROSSCHECK-001, NCT06994676), so as an enrollment target it is guideline-consonant. Unlike the donor and autologous TCR-T handles it is off-the-shelf, so there is no cell-manufacturing wait, and as a CD3 engager it can in principle work on the active marrow rather than only as post-transplant consolidation. Prior allo-HCT is allowed once 60 days have passed, which fits her. What keeps it at rank 4 on my axis: it is first-in-human with no efficacy or safety readout, it carries no consensus category of its own, and it is gated on the same pending HLA-A*02:01 typing as the rest of that axis.
primary_concerns: First-in-human, no clinical readout yet; a novel agent with no results has no consensus category, so the only guideline support is the general 'enroll in a trial' preference, not the agent itself.
Eligibility is gated on HLA-A*02:01, still pending typing; without that result she is not a confirmed-eligible patient for this trial.
As a CD3-engaging bispecific the expected class toxicity is cytokine release, and no organ-function or fitness workup is on file to size that risk.

picks.intervention_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) for AML relapse after allo-HCT
picks.rationale: Sibling DLI sits squarely inside ELN 2022's framing of post-transplant relapse: immunosuppression taper plus cytoreduction plus adoptive cellular therapy is the combination they credit with occasional durable remissions. Her late relapse (>5 months, here ~6 years) is exactly the feature that predicts DLI benefit in the EBMT series (Schmid 2007, pmid 17909197; 21% vs 9% 2-year OS with vs without DLI). The catch is burden: given in active high-burden disease, that same series shows ~15% 2-year OS, so DLI has to follow cytoreduction, not lead it. I treat it as an adjunct to the transplant platform, not a standalone.
primary_concerns: At 85% blasts she is in the active-disease/high-burden DLI group where the registry outcome is worst; DLI alone is not defensible here.
GVHD is the characteristic toxicity and would complicate a subsequent HCT2.
The registry benefit is a minority effect and selection-confounded; it calibrates expectations rather than promising much.

notes: Re-run over the full option set after CBX-250 was added. CBX-250 enters at rank 4: it is on the patient's A*02:01 axis and a recruiting trial, so it earns the general NCCN/ELN 'enroll in a trial' preference, and its off-the-shelf format plus potential activity on the active marrow give it an edge over DLI, which needs low burden to work; but it is first-in-human with no results and no consensus category, so it sits below the on-label and platform picks. Iomab-B (SIERRA, pmid 39298738) stays off the ranked list: phase 3 durable-CR signal for carrying an active high-blast marrow into transplant, but CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning is not NCCN/ELN-adopted and the pivotal population was heading to a first HCT, so it is a trial-route platform option (NCT07157514), not a consensus one. Rezatapopt stays off on guideline-fit: doubly contingent (confirm TP53, then confirm Y220C) with the only myeloid trial (NCT06616636) posting no results and PYNNACLE solid-tumor only. Eprenetapopt is worse for consensus (pan-reactivator, phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its endpoint, myeloid development largely halted). The whole plan hinges on pending workup: resolve TP53 (2019 report + p53 IHC + 17p FISH), pull HLA-A*02:01 and HA-1/HA-2 genotypes on patient and sibling, and confirm recipient-origin relapse by sorted-CD34 STR chimerism before any cellular option moves from 'undetermined' to eligible. Guideline version cited as NCCN AML v3.2026, the current published version (JNCCN Insights v3.2026); prior run's 'v4.2026' was corrected down.

picks.intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager; CROSSCHECK-001, NCT06994676)
picks.rationale: This is the closest match to what the patient actually asked for: an HLA-A*02:01-restricted immunotherapy, recruiting now, that they can travel for. Its edge over the TCR-T options is practical rather than theoretical — off-the-shelf, so no autologous or donor cell-manufacturing lead time, and prior allo-HCT is explicitly permitted once 60 days have passed, which fits a post-transplant relapse. I rank it first on the primary axis while naming the caveats plainly: it is phase 1 first-in-human with no efficacy readout, it carries the T-cell-engager CRS risk, and it sits behind the same pending HLA-A*02:01 typing as every other pick on this axis — the one records pull that unlocks all of them.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: the stated primary axis (HLA-A*02:01-restricted immunotherapy), curative intent, prefers_trials incl. travel, no toxicity veto, efficacy lean
In tension: phase 1 FIH, no efficacy yet, CRS risk expected for a CD3 engager; a lower evidence tier than the HA-1 TCR-T precedent
Gated on the same pending HLA-A*02:01 typing; unlike the TCR-T picks it does NOT require the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch or an HCT2 platform, which is why it can move fastest once A*02:01 is confirmed

picks.intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2-directed donor TCR-T after second allo-HCT (Bleakley platform; TSC-100/TSC-101, ALLOHA NCT05473910)
picks.rationale: This is the handle the case was originally submitted for, and it fits the patient's terms: curative intent, a trial they will travel for, and a graft-versus-leukemia mechanism that spares the tissues that drive GVHD. Bleakley's phase 1 got 4 of 9 recurrent post-HCT patients into CR with no dose-limiting toxicity, and TSC-100/101 runs the same mechanism on the back of a fresh matched transplant — a deeper published precedent than CBX-250, which is why the two sit close at the top. The catch is a heavier eligibility gate: HLA-A*02:01, a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor-negative mismatch genotyped in both the patient and the sibling, and recipient-origin relapse confirmed by sorted-CD34 STR chimerism. It ranks just behind CBX-250 only because that gate is longer and it needs the HCT2 platform under it, not because the mechanism is weaker.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: primary axis, curative intent, prefers_trials incl. travel, no veto, efficacy lean
In tension: three-part eligibility gate — A*02:01 typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient AND sibling, and sorted-CD34 STR chimerism for recipient origin — all unresolved
Sequencing: delivered on the back of HCT2 (rank 3), so it inherits that platform's timeline

picks.intervention_label: Targeted radioimmunotherapy conditioning (Iomab-B / 131I-apamistamab) into second allo-HCT; FLAMSA-RIC as the sequencing alternative
picks.rationale: The HA-1/HA-2 cells at rank 2 need a transplant under them, so honoring that side of the primary axis means getting the patient safely to HCT2 with an 85%-blast marrow. SIERRA is the strongest evidence that CD45-targeted radioimmunotherapy can carry active R/R AML into an allograft (durable CR 17% vs 0%), and FLAMSA-RIC reaches the same endpoint by sequencing; the roughly 6-year remission after the first transplant puts this patient in the more favorable band of the HCT2 registry (about 37% 2-year OS in the related-donor subgroup). Curative intent, a modality the patient kept explicitly on the table, no veto — the open axis is fitness, which is undocumented and should set conditioning intensity. Note this platform is not required for CBX-250, so if the marrow proves hard to control the T-cell engager remains a route that does not depend on it.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: curative intent, HCT2 explicitly acceptable, no veto, efficacy lean
In tension: SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a FIRST transplant, so prior-HCT eligibility for the go-forward apamistamab study (NCT07157514) must be verified
Open axis flagged in the patient's own file: no ECOG/cardiac/organ-function data yet; the 0.75 efficacy weight should be revisited once fitness is known

picks.intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (CD123 ADC) as cytoreductive bridge to HCT2 / cellular consolidation
picks.rationale: To reach a transplant or a cellular consolidation you first have to bring an 85%-blast marrow down, and re-running the FLAG-IDA scaffold the disease already failed is not the way. Pivekimab is a CD123 ADC with single-agent activity in R/R AML (ORR 21%) against the patient's confirmed CD123-positive blasts, without stacking onto a backbone that has already lost. It clears the preference filter — no veto, trial-acceptable — with two honest caveats: quantitative CD123 antigen density is still pending and would sharpen the choice, and the veno-occlusive signal matters with a transplant ahead. Tagraxofusp is a reasonable alternative but carries capillary-leak risk that argues for fitness data before committing.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: efficacy-leaning bridge, no veto, trial route available
In tension: quantitative CD123 density (requested) not yet back; VOD signal is relevant with HCT2 planned
Role is cytoreduction, not cure on its own — it earns its rank as a bridge to ranks 1-3, and it would also buy time to the CBX-250 slot

picks.intervention_label: WT1 HLA-A*02:01 TCR-T (WT1-TCRc4 / FH-WT1-E50); A*24:02 WT1-siTCR as the fallback lever
picks.rationale: If the HA-1/HA-2 pair does not mismatch but the patient is A*02:01-positive, WT1 keeps the HLA-restricted axis alive rather than foreclosing it — a second lever on the same primary reason for the run. The Chapuis WT1-TCRc4 work held 12 high-risk AML patients relapse-free post-transplant, and FH-WT1-E50 carries the current version, best positioned as post-cytoreduction or post-HCT2 consolidation rather than for florid relapse. If A*02:01 comes back negative, A*24:02 opens the WT1-siTCR lever, which is why both alleles should be typed in parallel before anyone forecloses this pathway. Same preference fit as the top picks, with a prophylaxis/MRD evidence base and a disease-state mismatch at the current blast burden.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: same HLA-restricted, curative-intent, trial-acceptable profile the run was built around
In tension: prophylaxis/MRD evidence, not active-relapse salvage; gated on A*02:01 (or A*24:02), still pending
Kept explicitly so an A*02:01-positive but HA-non-mismatched result does not close the immunotherapy axis the patient prioritized

picks.intervention_label: Dual CD33/CD123 compound CAR-T (antigen-escape hedge); on-label gemtuzumab as the available CD33 alternative
picks.rationale: Given the clonal evolution documented between 2019 and 2026, single-antigen cytoreduction invites escape, and the patient carries both CD33 and CD123. A compound CD33/CD123 CAR-T covers both antigens and is the escape hedge the profile flags — trial-acceptable and consistent with the curative goal. The honesty here is real: it is early-phase with xenograft-only support, no post-allo-HCT data, and CRS plus prior-transplant eligibility are open. On-label gemtuzumab is the lower-ceiling but immediately available CD33 option if a trial slot does not materialize.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: no veto, trial-acceptable, curative-intent framing
In tension: earliest-phase evidence of any pick; xenograft-only, no post-HCT data, CRS and prior-transplant eligibility unresolved
Quantitative CD33/CD123 density (requested) would gate the ADC/CAR decision it depends on

notes: Re-run over the full current option set after cbx-250 (CBX-250, CROSSCHECK-001) was added. I moved it to rank 1: it is squarely on the stated primary axis, recruiting now, off-the-shelf with no cell-manufacturing lead time, and prior-HCT is permitted — so it can move fastest once A*02:01 is confirmed, and unlike the HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T it needs neither the mismatch genotyping nor the HCT2 platform. Honest ordering, not hype: it sits above the Bleakley HA-1 TCR-T (rank 2) on speed and practical fit, not on evidence depth, and its confidence is low precisely because it is phase 1 FIH with no efficacy and a CRS risk. Deliberately did NOT foreground TP53/rezatapopt — doubly contingent (confirm the aberration, then confirm Y220C) and off the HLA-restricted axis; resolve it in parallel but it is not a preference-carrying pick today. Not a yes-machine on the 0.75 efficacy weight either: the patient's own file flags no ECOG/cardiac/organ-function data yet, so the efficacy lean and the conditioning intensity for ranks 3-4 should be revisited once fitness is assessed. The single load-bearing next action that unlocks the entire top of this list is a records pull, not a drug: retrieve the 2020 high-resolution HLA-A typing (and A*24:02 in parallel), genotype HA-1/HA-2 in the patient and sibling donor, and run STR chimerism on sorted CD34+ blasts to confirm recipient-origin relapse.
